advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether the reuse marker / original runner provenance should be persisted into the signed completion manifest, or document that reuse deliberately re-signs with runner='reused'.
evidence: transition_close.py:129-130: manifest only carries `f"model: {result.get('model') or 'n/a'}"` and `f"runner: {result.get('runner') or 'n/a'}"` — `reuse_provenance` is never consumed by `_verdict_manifest`
advisory.finding: The reuse path returns `reuse_provenance` and `runner='reused'` on the in-memory result, but `_verdict_manifest` (transition_close.py:126-134) only signs `runner`/`model` and does not read `reuse_provenance`; the durable re-signed op-cert therefore records `runner: reused` and loses the original provider's runner provenance and the reuse marker, so audit of a signed attestation cannot tell it was a reuse or which runner originally produced the PASS.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert the reuse-path result payload fields (runner='reused', coverage.attestation_reused=True, reuse_provenance runner/model, model from manifest) on a reuse case.
evidence: Source constructs distinctive fields: `"runner": "reused"`, `"coverage": {"llm_ran": False, "attestation_reused": True}` (close_autoresume.py:166,171) and `result["reuse_provenance"] = {"runner": prior_runner, "model": result["model"]}` (close_autoresume.py:175)

CLI test asserts only `assert calls == []`, `status == "closed"`, `closed_signature["verdict"] == "certified"`, `verified_at_sha == target`, and `latest_pass_record(...) is not None` (test lines 145-152) — none of which target the reuse-specific payload
`reuse_provenance` appears only at close_autoresume.py:175 in source and nowhere in tests (search_files)
advisory.finding: The reuse-result payload metadata introduced by the diff (runner='reused', coverage={'llm_ran':False,'attestation_reused':True}, reuse_provenance, and model extracted from the authenticated manifest via _manifest_value) is never asserted by any test. The CLI happy-path test only checks calls==[], status closed, the re-signed certified verdict, verified_at_sha, and latest_pass_record presence — all of which would also hold if the fresh provider ran. A regression that dropped or mislabeled these reuse fields would not be caught.
scenarios: A refactor that stops populating coverage.attestation_reused or reuse_provenance, or that sources model from the wrong place, passes all tests
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_cli_close_reuses_valid_same_ref_completion_attestation (or a direct _reusable_attested_pass unit test), assert the returned verdict dict carries runner=='reused', coverage=={'llm_ran':False,'attestation_reused':True}, and reuse_provenance=={'runner':'stored-runner','model':'stored-model'}.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a case where the manifest pins a verified_at_sha that differs from the op-cert's authenticated head and assert fresh verification runs.
evidence: Source guard: `if not signed_sha or signed_sha != authenticated_head: return None` (close_autoresume.py:138-139) with rationale comment that accepting the implicit HEAD fallback 'would let an old/missing verified-at-sha manifest qualify accidentally'

Parametrization cases are (FAIL,True,True),(PASS,False,True),(PASS,True,False) (test lines 187-189) — include_sha=False hits only the `not signed_sha` half; none pin a sha that differs from authenticated_head
Source: `if not isinstance(certified.get("signed_manifest"), list): return None` (close_autoresume.py:127-128) with rationale that legacy op-certs' plaintext mirror is insufficient
No test in the file sets up a certified verify_signature result whose signed_manifest is absent/non-list; the unverifiable test instead returns verified=False (test lines 289-296)
advisory.finding: The 'signed_sha != authenticated_head' rejection branch (a distinct defensive guard with explicit rationale) is not exercised. The parametrized include_sha=False case only reaches the `not signed_sha` sub-condition; no test constructs a manifest whose pinned verified_at_sha is present but disagrees with the op-cert's authenticated head, so that mismatch sub-branch has no regression coverage.
merged_from: The legacy op-cert guard 'signed_manifest not a list' (close_autoresume.py:127-128) has no dedicated test forcing that specific rejection path; the comment marks it as a deliberate correctness barrier (legacy op-certs predating manifest binding), yet no test constructs a certified record lacking a list-typed signed_manifest.
scenarios: A change that drops the `signed_sha != authenticated_head` clause, keeping only `not signed_sha`, would still pass every current test yet allow reuse of a manifest whose pin disagrees with the signed head
